description: Fifteen days of messages for one simulated user, built to test WHEN memory should be forgotten (professor's feedback). Order 1 (Ninja Van) ends early with a 'delivered' message (an ending event); order 2 (J&T) arrives silently on day 8 (only a re-check can catch it). Each fake cash-on-delivery text comes from the SAME courier as the remembered order and arrives while a 5-day memory of 'expecting a parcel' is still unexpired, so only staleness decides the outcome. 'completes' marks the situation that genuinely ends at that message; the simulated user uses it to answer 'forget this?' offers. Revised after the first live run: the 'delivered' message now has the user still expecting that parcel, and couriers are consistent within each order.

sessions.label: legit
sessions.text: Ninja Van: Your COD parcel (SGD 48.90) will arrive on Wed between 2-6pm. Please prepare exact cash for the driver.
sessions.note: Order 1 announced. User says yes; SecondLook offers to remember.

sessions.label: legit
sessions.text: Ninja Van: Your COD parcel (SGD 48.90) is out for delivery today. Please prepare exact cash for the driver.
sessions.note: Memory is fresh, so no question is needed.

sessions.label: legit
sessions.text: Ninja Van: Your parcel has been delivered. Thank you for choosing Ninja Van.
sessions.note: Order 1 arrives - an ending event. Genuine and asks for nothing.

sessions.label: scam
sessions.text: Ninja Van: Your COD parcel (SGD 63.40) will arrive today between 2-6pm. Please prepare exact cash for the driver.
sessions.note: Fake COD from the same courier inside the 5-day window. Fixed expiry still trusts 'expecting a parcel'.

sessions.note: Unrelated type: delivery memory must not leak into job messages.
